capabilities: Auto-scroll notes at adjustable speed with countdown timer and mirror flipping
Follow the reader's voice with on-device speech recognition and word highlighting
Control playback from Stream Deck, a mobile web remote, or keyboard commands
Read scripts aloud with offline or ElevenLabs text-to-speech
Integrate script playback with OBS recording via a local WebSocket API
extras: Marked as not manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. ElevenLabs TTS is a paid, opt-in cloud service that sends script text off-device; all other engines run offline. Detailed docs (Stream Deck actions, WebSocket API, TTS setup, troubleshooting) live in separate files rather than the README.
motivation: Designed for creators who already live in Obsidian and want a teleprompter that speaks the same Markdown they write in.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to read a note as a scrolling script while recording video, presenting, or practicing a speech.

relations.evidence: The voice-tracking matcher (speech-to-script alignment) is ported from jlecomte/voice-activated-teleprompter (MIT)
ElevenLabs (optional, cloud, paid — bring your own key)
OBS integration — start/stop recording synced with teleprompter playback
Stream Deck integration — 55+ actions across 8 categories with real-time bidirectional state sync

requires.name: Python venv for Kokoro MLX TTS

summary: Teleprompter view that auto-scrolls notes with voice tracking, text-to-speech, Stream Deck and mobile remote control, and OBS sync.
